external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: franchise stores
external_entities.description: Franchise stores whose colleagues are allowed to sign in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise colleagues' own identity provider that vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: The broker signs colleagues in, issues tokens, validates federated sign-ins, signs tokens, and supplies public signing keys.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token group membership to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

processes.name: HR system
processes.description: The system that supplies changes to colleague and group membership information overnight.
processes.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the broker to sign tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The broker's directory of colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: federated sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using a sign-in vouched for by the franchise identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token is valid for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before it expires.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: use token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the token to the store admin console, which decides permitted actions from the groups in the token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.notes: Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token signing key

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls overnight changes to colleagues and group membership from the HR system.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight process is how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: update membership
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group membership information in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs the tokens for every application.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: colleagues' own devices
trust_boundaries.description: The home devices colleagues use to sign in from home.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-controlled environment associated with franchise colleagues and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

trust_boundaries.name: HR system
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing the HR system; the source does not state its network location or authority relationship.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it contains colleague identity information and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token signing key.
assumptions.basis: The key store holds a signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it records colleague sign-ins.
assumptions.basis: The audit log records sign-ins, which identify authentication activity.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because the source calls it a console used by colleagues as an application.
assumptions.basis: The procedure defines a console as a web application interface.
